title: Constantinople 1453: The Last Walls

source_integrity.primary_source_or_tradition: Siege and fall of Constantinople, 1453; primary accounts differ

scenes.caption: What if the walls that protected a city for centuries could finally be breached? For centuries Constantinople stood behind formidable walls. In 1453, Sultan Mehmed II brought an Ottoman army to besiege the capital of the diminished Byzantine Empire.
historical_constraints: Byzantine defenders hold the walls; the Ottoman army remains outside the fortifications
do not depict Byzantine soldiers attacking their own walls
scenes.image_prompt: Vertical cinematic crop of a coherent sequential Byzantine icon mosaic meets Ottoman miniature panorama, gold tesserae, cobalt walls. Scene: vast Theodosian walls, Golden Horn and advancing army. The source story is Constantinople 1453: The Last Walls. Reuse exact character designs and border motifs from references/style_board.png; narrative relief/illustration, no modern objects, no printed captions or illegible text, no photorealistic cinematic actors.

scenes.caption: Large cannons battered defenses once thought impregnable. The defenders repaired breaches repeatedly, short of men and hope of substantial relief.
required_visuals: giant bronze bombard facing pitted walls
historical_constraints: Ottoman artillery fires toward the Theodosian walls; Byzantine defenders repair the damage
do not reverse the attacking and defending sides

scenes.caption: A chain helped defend the Golden Horn. Ottoman forces moved ships overland into the inlet, adding pressure from a direction the city feared.
required_visuals: ships on greased timbers above hills into harbor
historical_constraints: Ottoman forces move ships overland into the Golden Horn while defenders observe from the city
do not show Byzantine forces dragging the Ottoman fleet

scenes.caption: After weeks of siege, the Ottomans launched a major attack on May twenty-ninth. The defenses broke, and the Byzantine capital fell.
required_visuals: pre-dawn siege ladders and breach at walls
historical_constraints: Ottoman attackers assault the breach and Byzantine defenders resist from the walls
do not show the defenders attacking their own fortifications

scenes.caption: Constantine the Eleventh died during the fighting, though accounts vary about the exact circumstances. His empire ended with the city.
historical_constraints: preserve uncertainty about the exact circumstances of Constantine XI's death
do not depict a fabricated final duel or a confirmed identifiable death scene

scenes.caption: Mehmed entered Constantinople, which became the Ottoman imperial capital. What ended for one state became a beginning for another—and a turning point in Mediterranean history.
required_visuals: split image of cathedral domes and Ottoman imperial skyline
historical_constraints: show the transition from Byzantine rule to Ottoman imperial rule without erasing the city's layered history
do not depict the new capital as an ahistorical modern skyline
